questions.text: 1. What mass (kg) must be hung from a spring of stiffness 10 N/m to obtain a pendulum with an oscillation period of 1 s? π2 = 10.
2. A 200 g weight hanging from a spring makes 30 oscillations per minute. What is the spring constant (N/m)? π2 = 10.
3. A weight hanging from a spring of stiffness 200 N/m made 10 oscillations in 8 s. What is the mass of the weight (kg)? π2 = 10.
4. A spring pendulum was moved from the Earth to a planet where the acceleration due to gravity is 4 times that on Earth. How does its oscillation period change?
5. How will the period change for a spring pendulum with period T if the mass of the hanging weight is increased n times?
6. How does the period of longitudinal oscillations of a weight on a spring (spring pendulum) change if the mass of the weight increases 9 times?
7. How will the period of a spring pendulum change if the spring is shortened by half and the mass of the weight is doubled?
8. The oscillation period of the system in Figure 1 is 10 s, and in Figure 2 it is 8 s. Find the oscillation period of the weight in Figure 3 (s). All springs have the same stiffness.
9. Find the ratio of the periods T1/T2 of the spring pendulums shown in the figure: 1) k, 3k (in parallel); 2) 2k, 2k (in series), mass 4m.
10. Under the action of a hanging weight, a spring stretched by 2.5 cm. Determine the oscillation frequency of this spring pendulum (Hz).
